newsitem.title: USA: Dow Q1 hurt by forex, sees better pricing.
newsitem.headline: Dow Q1 hurt by forex, sees better pricing.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said first-quarter sales volume grew two percent, while selling prices declined by two percent due to a negative currency impact of about $100 million.

"The strong U.S. dollar played a significant role in the price decline we experienced in the first quarter," said chief executive William Stavropoulos. "However, when we adjust for this currency impact, we actually see positive pricing trends in many of our key products."
During the quarter, Dow said it experienced a mixed pricing scenario.

"Prices in some key products, notably polyethylene and vinyl chloride monomer, were up substantially from a year ago. Other products, such as caustic soda and polystyrene faced price declines," the company said.
The chemicals giant on Thursday reported first-quarter 1997 sales of $5.0 billion, net income of $452 million and earnings per share of $1.90.

Productivity, value growth initiatives, business portfolio restructuring and lower costs offset about $200 million of the more than $300 million impact of higher feedstock costs and the unfavorable currency impact on sales, Dow said.
As a result, operating income for the quarter was down only $103 million to $765 million from $868 million a year ago, the company said.

Operating expenses for the quarter were down 16 percent to $627 million compared to $743 million for same period a year ago. The reduction was achieved primarily through a combination of on-going productivity gains, lower costs, and the overall impact of currency on costs.

"As we head into the second quarter, favorable global economic conditions will support solid volume growth in our businesses. Lower feedstock costs and price stability in some key products, coupled with the on-going implementation of our productivity and value-growth initiatives, should result in a strong quarter for Dow," Stavropoulos said.
